why: An agent reads its instruction file whole, fenced blocks included, and a fenced command in AGENTS.md is an instruction to run it. The fail side is AGENTS.md with a sh fence that starts the Gemini CLI with its approval switch off. The pass side puts the byte-identical text in docs/setup.md, a document no agent loads by name: a fenced command there is only a warning (passed with a note), and the same words in prose would be nothing. Whoever skips fences in agent files turns the fail side green; whoever fails fenced examples in ordinary docs turns the pass side red.
